'''Arlene Paige Maclin''' is an American physicist and academic administrator. Maclin was one of the first African American women to receive a PhD in physics.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Roberson|first=Stephen|date=2021-02-13|title=February 13, 2021 - The First Five - National Society of Black Physicists|url=https://nsbp.org/blogpost/1914810/365664/February-13-2021--The-First-Five|url-status=live|access-date=2021-05-19|website=nsbp.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210519141018/https://nsbp.org/blogpost/1914810/365664/February-13-2021--The-First-Five |archive-date=2021-05-19 }}</ref> She is a professor at [[Howard University]].

== Early life and education ==
Maclin was born in [[Rawlings, Virginia]] on June 7, 1945.<ref name="History Makers"/> She earned her B.S. in [[engineering physics]] from [[North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University]] in 1967.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |title=N.C. A&T Alumna Leads the Way for Students to have Global Opportunities in STEM |url=https://relations.ncat.edu/pubs/alumnitimes/2017/nov22/arlenemaclin.html |work=N.C. A&T Alumni Times |date=November 22, 2017}}</ref> She was an undergraduate research assistant.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1965-08-07|title=For the cause of physics|work=The Pittsburgh Courier|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/38486937|access-date=2021-05-19}}</ref> After graduating, she spent time as a post-baccalaureate fellow at [[Bryn Mawr College|Bryn Mawr]] and [[Haverford College]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Personnel {{!}} Howard University Partnership Development and Design|url=https://hupdd.org/personnel/|access-date=2021-05-19|language=en-US}}</ref>

She completed a M.S. in theoretical [[nuclear physics]] from the [[University of Virginia]] in 1971,<ref>{{Cite book|last=Maclin|first=Arlene Paige|url=http://catalog.hathitrust.org/api/volumes/oclc/7259488.html|title=Charge-exchange scattering of pions on light nuclei|date=1971|language=English|oclc=988088208}}</ref> and a Ph.D. in theoretical solid state physics from [[Howard University]] in 1974.<ref name="History Makers">{{cite web|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/arlene-maclin|work=The History Makers |title=Arlene Maclin |date=January 2013 |access-date=2021-02-27}}</ref>

== Career ==
Maclin was a research scientist at MIT's [[Lincoln Laboratory]] and a visiting scientist at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] before she was appointed to serve as program director at the [[National Science Foundation]] in 1980. Between 1981 and 1983, she served as Senior Applied Research Physicist at the [[Central Intelligence Agency]].<ref name="History Makers"/>

Maclin is a professor at Howard University.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Poffenberger |first1=Leah |title=Making Room in Physics for Everyone |url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201805/room.cfm |journal=APS News |date=May 2018 |volume=27 |issue=5 |language=en}}</ref> She has also served as an academic administrator at [[Morgan State University]]<ref>{{Cite news|date=1976-03-18|title=Morgan board names 4 to administrative jobs|work=The Baltimore Sun|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/377504758/|access-date=2021-05-19}}</ref> and [[Hampton University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Women & Hi Tech - Grown from STEM: February Edition - Women & Hi Tech Celebrates "Equity and Inclusion" in 20th Year of The Leading Light Awards|url=https://www.womenandhitech.org/Blog/8764766|access-date=2021-05-19|website=www.womenandhitech.org}}</ref> She served as Delta Sigma Theta Distinguished Professor at [[Bennett University]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=7th International Conference on Women in Physics: U.S. Delegation|url=http://uswip.org/7th/Delegation.html#Maclin|access-date=2021-05-19|website=uswip.org}}</ref> She has developed an optical engineering program at [[Norfolk State University]] with a graduation rate of 96% and a high-quality laboratory equipment.<ref name=":0" /> She has developed science education programs for elementary and high school students as well, and collaborated with educators abroad to improve  student retention in scientific fields.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Maclin|first1=Arlene|last2=Wilkins|first2=Gregory|last3=Honkanen|first3=Seppo|last4=Kupinski|first4=Meredith|title=U.S.-Finland Planning Visit: Cooperative Research and Education Activities in Integrated Access Networks|url=https://grantome.com/grant/NSF/OISE-1042309|work=Grantome|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Maclin|first1=Arlene|last2=Johnson|first2=Mary|last3=Coleman|first3=Winson|last4=Johnson|first4=Mildred|title=District of Columbia Science & Engineering Regional Center for Minorities|url=https://grantome.com/grant/NSF/HRD-9053951|work=Grantome|language=en}}</ref> Based on successful models at Howard University, she presented results to the Department of Education to apply throughout the United States. Initiatives including pairing incoming students with those in the graduating class and creating more research project opportunities.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-08-21|title=Department of Education Selects Howard for Model Undergraduate STEM Research Program|url=https://newsroom.howard.edu/newsroom/static/7541/department-education-selects-howard-model-undergraduate-stem-research-program|access-date=2021-05-19|website=Howard Newsroom|language=en}}</ref>

Maclin acts as a mentor to undergraduate students, encouraging them to accept internship opportunities and helping them to find such positions. Though physics undergraduate classes are gradually becoming more diverse, faculty makeup at major institutions does not always reflect this change and Maclin believes that students should work together to support each other to create an environment that is comfortable for all.<ref name=":1" /> Minority students leave physics because they feel isolated and out of place, not because they are struggling academically.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Cole|first=KC|date=2004-04-14|title=Physics losing minorities|work=Albuquerque Journal|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/463273268|access-date=2021-05-19}}</ref>

She has represented the United States in delegations to the International Conference on Women in Physics.<ref name=":2" /> As early as 1975, Maclin delivered public lectures about computers and privacy issues.<ref>{{Cite news|last=DuPont|first=Alice|date=1975-04-04|title=FAMU looks at 'nosy' computers|work=Tallahassee Democrat|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/245844721|access-date=2021-05-19}}</ref>

==Research and publications ==

Maclin's research covers topics like fiber optical-electronic systems to achieve optical switching in semiconductors.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Maclin|first1=Arlene|last2=Simms|first2=Garfield|last3=Hu|first3=Liang|title=RIMI: Fiber Optic Sensors and Smart Materials|url=https://grantome.com/grant/NSF/HRD-9353126|work=Grantome|language=en}}</ref>

*Tsang T, Maclin AP. Velocity autocorrelation functions in model liquid metals. [[Physical Review]] A. 1975 Jan 1;11(1):360. According to [[Google Scholar]], it has been cited 7 times.<ref name="GS">[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C33&q=Arlene+Maclin&btnG=#d=gs_cit&u=%2Fscholar%3Fq%3Dinfo%3AnAAjXGujf5AJ%3Ascholar.google.com%2F%26output%3Dcite%26scirp%3D0%26hl%3Den] Google Scholar Author page, Accessed  Aug 14,  2021</ref>
*Maclin AP, Eisenberg JM. Charge-Exchange Scattering of Pions on 14N. Canadian Journal of Physics. 1971 Jul 1;49(13):1826-7 According to Google Scholar, this article has been cited  1 time <ref name=GS  />  
*Maclin AP. Work in progress-Globalization of science and engineering programs at Norfolk State University. In 2007 37th Annual Frontiers In Education Conference-Global Engineering: Knowledge Without Borders, Opportunities Without Passports 2007 Oct 10 (pp. T2A-16). IEEE.

== Awards and honours ==

* 2023 Howard Barnhill Distinguished Alumni Service Award from North Carolina Agricultural & State University
* 2025 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?y=2025&af=true|title=Fellows nominated in 2025|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2025-12-15}}</ref>
